name: anticoagulant reversal overview
title: Anticoagulant decision chart: the antithrombin-dependent injectables (unfractionated heparin, low molecular weight heparin, fondaparinux), the oral agents (warfarin, direct Xa inhibitors, dabigatran) and the IV direct thrombin inhibitors; each column gives when to choose it and when to avoid it, how to monitor it, and how to stop or reverse it

root.title: Anticoagulant: which one, how do I MONITOR it, and how do I REVERSE it?
lines: none of them with active bleeding, recent brain or spinal (CNS) surgery, or thrombocytopenia

groups.title: INDIRECT: need ANTITHROMBIN · injected
lines: the renal ones last longer in renal failure

groups.title: ORAL
lines: direct oral anticoagulants (Xa inhibitors, dabigatran): no monitoring, but P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 drugs raise or lower levels

head: h
Unfractionated heparin (UFH)
IIa + Xa · IV or subcutaneous (SC), hospital
half-life 60–90 min
rev: 1 mg per 100 U given in the last 2–2.5 h

head: h
Warfarin
vitamin K antagonist: no active II, VII, IX, X, protein C, S
half-life 36–42 h
mon: every 1–2 days at start → up to every 4–6 weeks
rev: VITAMIN K 2–10 mg IV + prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC)
vitamin K covers the rebound when PCC wears off

head: h
Dabigatran
oral direct thrombin (IIa) inhibitor
half-life 12–18 h
use: fixed dose, wide therapeutic window, fewer interactions than warfarin
rev: monoclonal antibody · emergency reversal only (very expensive)
